questions.q: In his vision, what did Amos see Yahweh doing when the second crop of the season was starting to grow?
questions.a: Amos saw Yahweh forming a locust swarm that would destroy the crop.

questions.q: What was Yahweh’s response when Amos asked him to forgive and not send the swarm of locusts to punish his people?
questions.a: Yahweh changed his mind and declared that this disaster would not happen.

questions.q: In his vision, what did Amos see Yahweh summoning to punish his people?
questions.a: Amos saw Yahweh bringing fire to punish his people.

questions.q: What was Yahweh’s response when Amos asked him not to bring fire to punish the people?
questions.a: Yahweh again relented and declared that this disaster would not happen either.

questions.q: In his vision, where did Amos see the Lord standing?
questions.a: Amos saw the Lord standing beside a wall with a plumb line in his hand.

questions.q: What did the Lord say was the meaning of the plumb line?
questions.a: The Lord said the plumb line meant he was going to test whether the Israelites were living rightly and this time, he would not hold back from punishing them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh declare he would do to Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh declared he would destroy the hilltop shrines and other holy places in Israel.

questions.q: What did Amaziah the priest accuse Amos of doing?
questions.a: Amaziah accused Amos of conspiring against Jeroboam, king of Israel.

questions.q: What had Amos prophesied about Jeroboam?
questions.a: Amos had prophesied that Jeroboam would be killed in battle.

questions.q: Where did Amaziah tell Amos to flee to if he wanted to continue to prophesy?
questions.a: Amos was told to flee to the land of Judah and prophesy there.

questions.q: What did Amaziah tell Amos not to do at Bethel?
questions.a: Amaziah told Amos not to prophesy at Bethel again, because it is the king’s sanctuary and a royal temple.

questions.q: What was Amos’ work before Yahweh took him to be his prophet?
questions.a: Amos was a herdsman and keeper of sycamore fig trees.

questions.q: Why did Amos leave his work tending a flock of sheep?
questions.a: Yahweh took him away from tending his sheep when he told him to go prophesy to the people of Israel.

questions.q: What did Amos say that Amaziah was telling him not to do?
questions.a: Amaziah was telling him not to prophesy against Israel or preach against the descendants of Isaac.

questions.q: What did Yahweh prophesy against Amaziah, priest of Bethel?
questions.a: Yahweh declared that Amaziah would die in an foreign land, his wife would be a prostitute, his sons and daughters would be killed, and his land would be divided up.

commentary.text: Visions of judgments to come upon Israel.

Verses 1–9 God bears long, but he will not bear always with a provoking people. The remembrance of the mercies we formerly received, like the produce of the earth of the former growth, should make us submissive to the will of God, when we meet with disappointments in the latter growth. The Lord has many ways of humbling a sinful nation. Whatever trouble we are under, we should be most earnest with God for the forgiveness of sin. Sin will soon make a great people small. What will become of Israel, if the hand that should raise him be stretched out against him? See the power of prayer. See what a blessing praying people are to a land. See how ready, how swift God is to show mercy; how he waits to be gracious. Israel was a wall, a strong wall, which God himself reared as a defence to his sanctuary. The Lord now seems to stand upon this wall. He measures it; it appears to be a bowing, bulging wall. Thus God would bring the people of Israel to the trial, would discover their wickedness; and the time will come, when those who have been spared often, shall be spared no longer. But the Lord still calls Israel his people. The repeated prayer and success of the prophet should lead us to seek the Saviour.

It is no new thing for the accusers of the brethren, to misrepresent them as enemies to the king and kingdom, as traitors to their prince, and troublers of the land, when they are the best friends to both. Those who make gain their godliness, and are governed by the hopes of wealth and preferment, are ready to think these the most powerful motives with others also. But those who have a warrant from God, like Amos, ought not to fear the face of man. If God, that sent him, had not strengthened him, he could not thus have set his face as a flint. The Lord often chooses the weak and foolish things of the world to confound the wise and mighty. But no fervent prayers, or self-denying labours, can bring proud sinners to bear faithful reproofs and warnings. And all who oppose or despise the Divine word, must expect fatal effects to their souls, unless they repent.
